newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries easier in Tokyo, trend stays weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries easier in Tokyo, trend stays weak.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly weaker by Tokyo midday on Monday due to light position squaring sales led by dealers, traders said.
Activity was dull amid a lack of strong factors, but the dollar's fall against the mark and the yen this morning slightly hurt prices, they said.

"Long holders were unloading some of their positions this morning due to the dollar's fall, but in general activity was quiet," a Japanese commercial bank trader said. "With the exception of a series of auctions this week, there are no major indicators scheduled, so I expect prices to be range-bound."
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 94-19/32, yielding 7.06 percent, compared with 94-22/32 in New York.
The June T-bond futures contract was at 108-1/32, up 1/32 from the previous close.
Traders said the basic market undertone still stayed weak as rate rise fears persisted.

"With the market pricing-in another credit tightening and concerns over currency intervention capping the dollar's rise, many Japanese investors are becoming nervous about buying in any large volume," a Japanese brokerage trader said.
